memory_candidates.content: A shell function that scans a file line-by-line and prints findings (e.g. `nonconforming_phase_headings <file>`) must NOT be checked for "any output" via `func <file> | grep -q .` under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits after its first match and closes the read end of the pipe; if the producer is still writing (realistic whenever each loop iteration does non-trivial work like multiple greps per line), the producer receives SIGPIPE and, under pipefail, the pipeline's reported exit status becomes the producer's non-zero signal-exit code (141) rather than reliably reflecting whether output existed -- this silently and intermittently misclassifies 'findings exist' as 'no findings'. The fix is a dedicated boolean-check function that captures the full output via command substitution first (`findings="$(func <file>)"; [[ -n "$findings" ]]`), which reads to EOF and never triggers the race. Add a fixture test that runs the OLD racy idiom under `set -o pipefail` as a live regression guard/documentation of why the safe helper exists.

A doc-lint gate that extracts bare filenames from prose (e.g. via a regex like `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(sh|sql)\b`) and compares them against a manifest's declared script list must compare BASENAMES, not full path-prefixed strings, whenever the manifest can declare subdirectory-scoped entries (e.g. `lib/foo.sh`, `tests/bar.sh`). An exact-string comparison silently false-positives on any subdirectory-scoped script that gets referenced by its bare filename in a SKILL.md/agent.md/command doc -- a latent bug that stays invisible until the first such reference is ever written. When adding a check-extension-docs.sh-style cross-reference validator, build a basename-normalized fallback exclusion set alongside the exact-match one from the start.
